summary: Build a VAT calculation and invoicing app with country/product-category based VAT rules, including UK-specific zero/reduced handling, reverse charge, exports, exemptions, and compliant invoice wording/disclaimers.
architectural_notes: VAT calculation must follow strict priority order: Reverse Charge (only if B2B), then Export, then Exempt, then UK-specific zero/reduced, then EU reduced, else Standard.
Enforce eligibility-based VAT rates (no manual override); invalid reduced/zero selections must auto-fallback to Standard.
When productCategory is 'Others', VAT must always be Standard regardless of other inputs.
Invoice output should include computed rate/vatAmount/total plus a label, and separate invoice wording derived from label+country.
Unsupported country selection should raise a clear 'Country not supported' error.

existing_features.title: Update the VAT rate configuration so the app uses the provided country VAT rates (DE/FR/NL/PL/SE/IT/BE/AT/HU/ES/GB with GB zero=0) as the authoritative source for the smart VAT engine.

Implement the provided category eligibility database and use it in VAT calculations: UK zero-eligible list, UK reduced-eligible list, EU reduced-eligible list, and exempt categories list (exempt applies to all countries).

Amend the unified VAT engine to follow the exact priority order and behaviors specified: 1) Reverse Charge (only when vatCategory is reverse and transaction is B2B), 2) Export (if isExport is true), 3) Exempt (if productCategory is in exempt list), 4) Zero (UK only; if country is GB and productCategory is UK-zero eligible), 5) Reduced (UK reduced list when GB; EU reduced list otherwise), 6) Standard fallback.

Enforce auto-fallback protection: even if a user manually selects reduced/zero VAT categories, the VAT engine must automatically apply standard VAT whenever the selected product category is not eligible; no manual override is allowed.

Update the product category dropdown options to exactly match the requested UX list and keep prior dropdown rendering fixes intact (e.g., safe z-index/overflow classes and current dropdown behavior). The dropdown must include: Basic Food, Books, Medical, Transport, Hotel, Financial Services, Insurance, Education, Domestic Fuel (UK), Others.
Implement the UI/logic rule: when productCategory is 'Others', the VAT result must always be Standard VAT (even if the user selected reduced/zero in the VAT category/treatment controls).
Use the provided result builder output fields for VAT computation outputs (rate, vatAmount, total, label) and ensure the UI/invoice continues to display consistent results derived from these values.

Ensure professional invoice wording auto-switch uses the provided logic for Reverse Charge (localized for DE/FR/IT/GB with fallback) and English text for Exempt / Zero Rated / Reduced VAT / Standard VAT, based on the VAT label returned by the engine.

new_feature_requests.summary: Implement Smart VAT Engine with prioritized handling: Reverse Charge (B2B), Export (zero), Exempt, UK Zero, UK Reduced, EU Reduced, and Standard fallback
Add VAT rate configuration by country (DE/FR/NL/PL/SE/IT/BE/AT/HU/ES/GB with GB zero=0)
Add product category eligibility lists for UK zero, UK reduced, EU reduced, and global exempt categories
Add result builder to return clean output (rate, vatAmount, total, label)
Auto-generate professional invoice wording based on VAT label and country (reverse charge localized; exempt/zero/reduced/standard text)
Add auto-fallback protection: prevent manual reduced/zero misuse by enforcing eligibility; if not eligible then apply standard (no override)
Update UX dropdown product categories (Basic Food, Books, Medical, Transport, Hotel, Financial Services, Insurance, Education, Domestic Fuel (UK), Others) and enforce 'Others' => always Standard VAT
Add global legal disclaimer text to all invoices

Add the global legal disclaimer text to all generated invoices: "VAT calculated based on selected country, product category and transaction type. The supplier is responsible for verifying compliance with applicable VAT legislation."
